The Piano

I started playing the piano in 2015 as an extracurricular hobby, but it quickly became a true passion. What I enjoy most about this instrument is the freedom it offers. I can explore and perform a wide variety of pieces across different genres.

As someone passionate about video games and pop culture, I've always appreciated being able to choose the music I play and bring to life the pieces that inspire me personally.

Video Games

Hello! I'm Gabriel, and I've been passionate about programming since my first year of studies. Over the years, I have built experience in web development, software engineering, video game creation, and DevOps.

I enjoy exploring new technologies and appreciate how the ever-evolving field of IT constantly challenges me to learn and grow. I love the logical side of programming and thinking about how to design optimized, efficient solutions. I started playing the piano in 2015 as an extracurricular hobby, but it quickly became a true passion. What I enjoy most about this instrument is the freedom it offers. I can explore and perform a wide variety of pieces across different genres.

As someone passionate about video games and pop culture, I've always appreciated being able to choose the music I play and bring to life the pieces that inspire me personally.

Although I no longer take formal lessons, I still play regularly and continue learning on my own.

E-Sports

I'm passionate about competitive gaming and have been following the esports scene for years.

I particularly enjoy watching professional League of Legends tournaments and staying updated with the latest strategies and team developments, especially when it comes to Fnatic and Solary. I've had the chance to attend major offline events with crowds of over 10,000 people, which allowed me to experience the incredible energy and emotion of live esports, it was truly unforgettable.

Video games have been a significant part of my life since childhood. My very first game was Mario Kart DS, but as a kid, I mostly enjoyed watching my older sisters play and videos on youtube, which is what ignited my passion for gaming.

I enjoy a wide range of genres, from story-driven adventures to competitive multiplayer titles. While I'm a big fan of League of Legends, I also have a strong attachment to Nintendo franchises, especially 3D Mario games and The Legend of Zelda.

ABOUT ME

Hello! I'm Gabriel, and I've been passionate about programming since my first year of studies. Over the years, I have built experience in web development, software engineering, video game creation, and DevOps.

I enjoy exploring new technologies and appreciate how the ever-evolving field of IT constantly challenges me to learn and grow. I love the logical side of programming and thinking about how to design optimized, efficient solutions. I also take great pleasure in creating applications that are both user-friendly and visually appealing, reflecting my personal style.

In my free time, I'm passionate about video games, playing the piano, and esports. I also really enjoy socializing, expanding my knowledge, and developing my own perspectives on a wide range of topics.

The Piano

I started playing the piano in 2015 as an extracurricular hobby, but it quickly became a true passion. What I enjoy most about this instrument is the freedom it offers. I can explore and perform a wide variety of pieces across different genres.

As someone passionate about video games and pop culture, I've always appreciated being able to choose the music I play and bring to life the pieces that inspire me personally.

Although I no longer take formal lessons, I still play regularly and continue learning on my own.

E-Sports

I'm passionate about competitive gaming and have been following the esports scene for years.

I particularly enjoy watching professional League of Legends tournaments and staying updated with the latest strategies and team developments, especially when it comes to Fnatic and Solary. I've had the chance to attend major offline events with crowds of over 10,000 people, which allowed me to experience the incredible energy and emotion of live esports, it was truly unforgettable.

I'm also a big fan of the Super Smash Bros. scene, where I closely follow Glutonny. Although this scene is less professionalized, it offers a more authentic and grassroots side of esports that I truly appreciate for its passion, creativity, and strong sense of community.

Video Games

Video games have been a significant part of my life since childhood. My very first game was Mario Kart DS, but as a kid, I mostly enjoyed watching my older sisters play and videos on youtube, which is what ignited my passion for gaming.

I enjoy a wide range of genres, from story-driven adventures to competitive multiplayer titles. While I'm a big fan of League of Legends, I also have a strong attachment to Nintendo franchises, especially 3D Mario games and The Legend of Zelda.

For me, gaming isn’t just entertainment—it’s also a source of inspiration for my programming projects and creativity.

parts:
I analyzed only states and URLs actually reached through the Cloak Browser session. I did not guess routes or use prior knowledge. One limitation is material: the available Browser connector exposes navigation, rendered-page extraction, clicks/typing/keyboard, screenshots, downloads, and tabs, but no DevTools console, request log, raw response headers, cookie API, or local/session-storage API. Those areas are therefore explicitly marked unverified rather than inferred.

## 1. Site purpose and structure

`https://missclick.net/` is a personal developer portfolio for “Gabriel.” The rendered landing page describes experience in web development, software engineering, game development, and DevOps, plus hobbies including piano, esports, and video games.

The main header consistently exposes:

`Home` · `About Me` · `Skills` · `Hobbies` · `GitHub Stats` · `Projects` · `Contact` · `Login`

The landing content contains a terminal-styled hero with:

`$ npm install missclick`

and:

`+ missclick@07.11.04 added 1 package, and audited 2 packages in 3s`

followed by About/Hobbies content, role labels `FULL STACK`, `SOFTWARE`, `GAME DEV`, `DEVOPS`, a GitHub-themed/statistics area, and the CTA `Explore Projects`.

The footer exposes `Home`, `Discover`, and `© Missclick.net - 2025`.

## 2. Routes and states actually observed

| URL/state | Observed behavior |
|---|---|
| `https://missclick.net/` | HTTP 200, title `MissclickNet`. Main portfolio page. |
| `https://missclick.net/home` | HTTP 200. Renders substantially the same portfolio content as `/`. An additional visible `Loading...` state was observed. |
| `https://missclick.net/projects` | HTTP 200 on a later DOMContentLoaded navigation. Project browser with search, sort, tag filters and grid/list layouts. |
| `https://missclick.net/projects` loading state | Two `Loading...` placeholders were observable before the project data appeared. |
| `https://missclick.net/projects/admin` | This is the header `Login` link target. Navigating there ended at `https://missclick.net/login`; the intermediate redirect mechanism/status was not exposed. |
| `https://missclick.net/login` | Final HTTP 200. `Admin Login` form. |
| `https://missclick.net/#` | Header `Contact` destination. Navigation normalized to `https://missclick.net/`; I discovered no separate contact route or contact form. |

No internal per-project detail routes were discovered. Project cards point directly to external/project destinations.

The `/projects` loading behavior was reproducible. On one navigation, waiting for the browser `load` event timed out after the connector's 45-second bound; the page itself had reached `/projects` but still displayed two `Loading...` placeholders, and the projects subsequently appeared. On a later fresh DOMContentLoaded navigation, the placeholders were still present after six seconds and were populated after an additional ten seconds. This is an observation from the isolated browser environment, not a general performance benchmark.

## 3. Landing-page navigation and interaction

The rendered DOM extraction identifies the principal links as approximately:

`tag=a, name="Home", href="https://missclick.net/"`

`tag=a, name="Projects", href="https://missclick.net/projects"`

`tag=a, name="Contact", href="https://missclick.net/#"`

`tag=a, name="Login", href="https://missclick.net/projects/admin"`

The `About Me`, `Skills`, `Hobbies`, and `GitHub Stats` entries were returned as `a` elements whose extracted `href` was null. This is consistent with JavaScript-controlled section navigation, but the exact implementation was not exposed. Attempts to activate `About Me` through the automation connector failed its pointer-events check, so I cannot claim the actual click/scroll behavior.

Two buttons have accessible names `❮` and `❯`, corresponding to a carousel-like control. Activating `❯` caused no URL or textual change detectable by the page reader; a visual-only transition may have occurred, but that is not verified.

`Explore Projects` is a button rather than an extracted anchor. Activating it changed the URL from `/home` to `/projects`.

There is also an unnamed `input type="text"` in the terminal-styled landing area. I entered `help` and submitted it. The field accepted the input, but no visible text, route, or state change followed. No executable terminal behavior was discovered.

The `Contact` header link's actual extracted destination is `https://missclick.net/#`. Visiting it returned to the root page. No email field, message field, contact form, or separate contact content was discovered in the rendered page.

## 4. Projects page

After loading, I observed 15 project entries. The initial ordering was newest-first, beginning with `OR Recorder Transcriber — 2026-08` and ending with `Streaming Power — 2023-10`.

The main controls are:

`input type="text", name="Search projects..."`

`button "Sort"`

`button "Tags"`

`button "Grid view"`

`button "List view"`

Opening `Sort` exposed four buttons: `Newest first`, `Oldest first`, `A-Z`, and `Z-A`.

I exercised `Oldest first`. The URL remained `/projects`, while the order immediately changed to begin:

`Streaming Power — 2023-10`

`Carla Ros NS3 Bridge — 2024-07`

`FindWord — 2024-08`

and continued chronologically through `OR Recorder Transcriber — 2026-08`. Sorting is therefore observable client-side state rather than route navigation.

Opening `Tags` exposed:

`Data Science`, `Devops`, `Game`, `Library`, `Network`, `Simulation`, `Software`, `Website`.

Selecting `Software` kept the URL at `/projects`, changed the control to `Tags 1`, added `Clear all`, and reduced the displayed set to five projects:

`OR Recorder Transcriber`, `Ultimate Converter`, `Kaboom`, `Square Game`, and `Carla Ros NS3 Bridge`.

`Clear all` restored the complete collection.

Search is also live client-side filtering. Entering `XML` immediately reduced the collection to `XML RPC — 2026-02`; there was no submit operation or URL change.

Entering `zzzz-no-match` produced a dedicated empty state:

`No projects found`

`Try adjusting your search or filter criteria`

`Clear filters`

The `Clear filters` button restored the normal collection.

Grid and list views materially change the rendered representation. In grid view, project links were extracted as anchors with empty accessible names; technology lists were abbreviated, e.g. two technologies followed by `+4`. List view exposed the complete technology lists and gave every project destination the link text/accessibility name `View Project`.

For example, the list representation of `OR Recorder Transcriber` exposed:

`Whisper`, `Pyside6`, `Python`, `Faster-whisper`, `Pywhispercpp`, `Openai-whisper`.

The list representation of `Ultimate Converter` exposed:

`Flask`, `FFmpeg`, `Python`, `HTML`, `CSS`, `Docker`, `JavaScript`, `SpotDL`, `Youtube-dl`, `Inkscape`.

## 5. Project/resource inventory

These are the destinations actually exposed in the rendered `/projects` DOM:

| Project | Observed destination |
|---|---|
| OR Recorder Transcriber | `https://github.com/Gabrieleirbag1/OR-Recorder-Transcriber` |
| NOL Event Classifier | `https://github.com/Gabrieleirbag1/NOL-Event-Data-Classifier` |
| XML RPC | `https://www.npmjs.com/package/xml-rpc-ts` |
| GeoNovis | `https://geonovis.missclick.net/` |
| Lite Logging | `https://pypi.org/project/litelogging/` |
| KDLK Pi-Hole DNS Server | `https://missclick.net/` |
| KDLK Nextcloud | `https://nextcloud.missclick.net/` |
| Missclicknet | `https://missclick.net/` |
| KDLK Proxmox Server | `https://nextcloud.missclick.net/` |
| Ultimate Converter | `https://ultimate-converter.missclick.net/` |
| Kaboom | `https://github.com/Gabrieleirbag1/Kaboom/releases` |
| Square Game | `https://github.com/Gabrieleirbag1/Square-Game/releases` |
| FindWord | `https://findword.missclick.net/` |
| Carla Ros NS3 Bridge | `https://github.com/Gabrieleirbag1/CARLA-ROS-NS3` |
| Streaming Power | `https://streamingpower.missclick.net/streamingpower/` |

There are noteworthy duplicate destinations: `KDLK Pi-Hole DNS Server` and `Missclicknet` both point to the main site root, while `KDLK Nextcloud` and `KDLK Proxmox Server` both point to the Nextcloud subdomain. Whether these are intentional is not verified.

I exercised the `OR Recorder Transcriber` project link. It opened a second browser tab at its GitHub repository while leaving the `/projects` tab active. I did not generalize this behavior to every external link without testing each one.

## 6. Login form

Navigating to the header's `https://missclick.net/projects/admin` target ended at:

`https://missclick.net/login`

The rendered form is:

`Admin Login`

`Username`

`input type="text", name="Enter your username"`

`Password`

`input type="password", name="Enter your password"`

`button type="submit", name="Login"`

I tested only empty submission; I did not perform credential guessing. Submitting both fields empty remained at `/login` and displayed the generic message:

`Invalid username or password`
